# Appeal of Denial — Total Shoulder Replacement (CPT 23472)

**Governing Policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

**RE: Denial dated 2026-08-15 | Reference number: POC-209DEB4204-66822**
**Member: Taylor Jennings | Member ID: W164265496**
**Plan: 'Ohana Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), State of Hawaii**

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472). My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to walk through what my records actually show, because I believe this conclusion does not match my treatment history.

- I experienced 14 months of progressive shoulder pain that was not relieved by rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, from 2026-04-14 to 2026-06-23), focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-02, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI on 2026-06-19 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I currently cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion.

I have completed a structured course of physical therapy, medication management, and injection treatment, and my symptoms have not improved. A full-thickness rotator cuff tear with fatty atrophy is also a structural finding that does not resolve with continued conservative care.

## A note on the criteria quoted to me

I want to be transparent with the reviewer: the policy language I have been given to cite in support of this appeal is drawn from the "Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain" and related cervical spine sections of the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines. That language addresses neck and cervical spine surgery (for example, criteria involving cervical radiculopathy, myelopathy, and neurological signs like Hoffmann sign or Babinski sign). It does not address shoulder replacement or rotator cuff pathology, and I have not been provided with the specific section of the Evolent guidelines that applies to total shoulder replacement or rotator cuff repair. I am not quoting that cervical spine language here because it is not the applicable criteria for my procedure, and I do not want to misstate what the plan's policy says about my case.

## Request for the criteria actually applied

Because the specific criteria used to evaluate my shoulder replacement request have not been identified for me, I am asking the plan to provide, in writing, the exact section of the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines (or any other clinical review criteria) that was applied to deny CPT 23472 in my case. I understand that 'Ohana Health Plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review, and that Evolent publishes its criteria publicly without requiring a login. I would like the opportunity to review the specific conservative-care requirements for shoulder replacement so that I can show, point by point, how my records meet them.

## What I am asking for

I am asking the plan to reconsider the denial of my total shoulder replacement, to provide the specific shoulder-replacement criteria that were applied to my case, and to approve this surgery based on the documented failure of physical therapy, medication, and injection treatment, along with the structural findings on my MRI.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-11. I am submitting this appeal through the process described in my denial letter, and I understand I can also submit it at ambetterhealth.com (by selecting Hawaii and using the state's appeal/grievance form) or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Marchetti's office.

Sincerely,

[Patient signature]
Taylor Jennings
Member ID: W164265496
[Date]
[Patient contact information]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Anterior Cervical Discectomy with Fusion (ACDF) – Multiple Levels When one of the two following criteria are met (1–8):

○ Upper extremity weakness ○ Unsteady gait related to myelopathy/balance or generalized lower extremity weakness ○ Disturbance with coordination ○ Hyperreflexia ○ Hoffmann sign ○ Positive Babinski sign and/or clonus ● Progressive neurological deficit (motor deficit, bowel or bladder dysfunction) with corresponding evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on an MRI or CT scan images – immediate surgical evaluation is indicated When ALL of the following criteria are met (6–8):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy due to ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;
See Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Cervical Posterior Decompression with Fusion (CPDF) - Single Level When one of the two following criteria are met (1–8,11):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity OR documented pseudarthrosis of prior ACDF/Cervical Artificial Disc Replacement (CADR) - one of the most common indications for a Single Level or Multi Levels CPDF is a failed anterior procedure ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;
NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:

OR ○ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment.

See Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Criteria Cervical Fusion for Treatment of Axial Neck Pain Fusion In Individuals with Non-Radicular Cervical Pain ALL of the following criteria must be met (14,15):

● Improvement of the symptoms has failed or plateaued, and the residual symptoms of pain and functional disability are unacceptable at the end of 6 to 12 consecutive months of appropriate, active treatment, or at the end of longer duration of non- operative programs for those debilitated with complex problems NOTE:
● Cervical radiculopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;

preferred for examining bony structures, or in individuals presenting with clinical symptoms or signs inconsistent with MRI findings (e.g., foraminal compression not seen on MRI) As first-line treatment without conservative care measures in the following clinical cases (1,2,6,9):
○ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment;
OR ○ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment;
● Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at single level corresponding with the clinical findings.
